1.text: Prayer. A friend's excuses must be heard. C. --- Gr. "and he who apologises shall be preserved from ruin." Grabe adds, "how good it is for one who has been rebuked," &c. v. 4. H. --- Thus the guilty merit pardon, and the innocent obtain a greater reward, and satisfy for former offences. W.

2.text: Maiden. Or "woman," (H.) who has been entrusted to his care. M. --- Such people are not free from concupiscence, which must be restrained by the virtue of chastity. S. Aug. c. Jul. vi. 14.

8.text: Hated. As the pests of society. See Cic. off. 1.

9.text: Loss. The prosperity of the wicked must not be envied. Ps. xxxviii. 1, 8. C.

11.text: Glory. Galba "would have been universally deemed worthy of the empire, if he had not reigned." Tacit. Hist. 1. --- Adrian VI. thought the pontificate the greatest misfortune to which he had been exposed; and this observation ws engraven on his tomb. --- Estate. By merit.

12.text: Sevenfold. As the merchandise was good for nothing, which the miser had obtained for a little money, thinking to save thereby.

13.text: Graces. Or favours bestowed with ill-nature.

14.text: Sevenfold. He expects more. C. --- His intention is full of guile, who flattereth and detracteth for the sake of gain. W.

15.text: Much. As Dido did. "This is to make a display of favours to excite hatred." Sen. Ben.

16.text: Hateful. He seems to distrust you, and will not permit his goods to be of any service. C.

17.text: Have. Gr. "say I have," &c. --- His. Gr. "my," as also v. 18. H. --- Such is the language of the fool.

19.text: That, &c. Riches and poverty are both wrong to misers and fools. Gr. "he had as well be without any thing." C.

23.text: Shall. Gr. adds, "not." Yet if a person has had the will to offend, he must repent, though the could not put it in execution. H.

24.text: Himself. Being afraid to beg for necessaries, or given too much.

25.text: Nothing. People are always displeased, when a promise is broken. C.

26.text: Man. "It is the vice of slaves." Arist. Ethic.

27.text: Lying. He exposes honour and virtue, without making restitution. C. --- He throws all into confusion, and we can trust him with nothing. M.

29.text: A. Gr. adds a title, "discourses of proverbs."

30.text: And...exalted, is not in Gr. but explains the meaning of the former sentence. --- Escape. Gr. "obtain pardon for iniquity." H. --- The great will protect him.

31.text: Make. Gr. "like a bit in the mouth, remove corrections." Ex. xxiii. 8. C.

32.text: Both? He who, through a false humility refuses to take charge of others, resembles a man who locks up his corn in time of scarcity. S. Greg. Part. iii. 26. Matt. xxv. C. --- Wisdom must be shewn for the benefit of others. W.

33.text: Folly. He may still appear to have some sense, and injures none. --- It is convenient to conceal faults, provided they be amended. W.
